notes.title: ASTRALODE Freeminers v0.94 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Hey there! It's been an [i]awfully[/i] long time since this thing's been updated. There are a number of tweaks and changes I've been sitting on for an eternity, some small, some pretty big. They go a little like:

[list]
[*]Ore upgrading is now significantly more forgiving! Bombs can be safely detonated directly on ore, making it far easier to pull off an upgrading explosion and much harder to make an ore-ruining mistake. Burnt ore is the exception, a direct hit with a bomb will still ruin the ore if it has already been overcooked.
[*]An indicator of ore harvest & mining progress in the current asteroid now appears in the main game window below the ship, rather than needing to be checked in the pause menu (but the detailed list of exactly which ore have been collected still resides there in the pause menu).
[*]The origin of the Lazer Boomer's 4-pane AOE is repositioned to more sensibly align with where the tool makes contact with the obstacle
[*]Visual effects for ore harvest and ore ruin are now fancier.
[*]Sound effects for ore harvest and losing a tool are slightly louder.
[*]Spacing in the dialogue box has been reworked to accommodate 4 lines of text, now making it possible for longer strings of text to fit into a single page.
[*]A number of minor bugs in the menu have been fixed, such as settings refusing to reset to the correct defaults, some inconsistencies in setting titles, and layering issues with various game elements active below the pause menu.
[*]A bug where the Trainer Gainer goal would refuse to unlock even after a copilot was sufficiently levelled up is now fixed.
[*]A bug where a useless and unintended 0 kB config file would be created in the root directory on game launch fixed.
[*]Various edits made to text and dialogue to accommodate the change in bomb/ore mechanics.
[/list]
Added later via quiet patch (Jul 8, 2022 @ 4:37pm)
[list]
[*]A bug where the pause menu would be buggy and unusable while either the Atlas Mineralis or Certification Guide subscreens were open fixed.
[*]A bugged and glitchy layout of the failure screen when too much ore has been ruined has been fixed, caused by the recently introduced ore harvest & mining progress on-screen indicator improperly disabling.
[*]Wonky text alignment of goal descriptions on the Certification Guide subscreen fixed.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/b46d9cdde246ba9a972d55c36bc4794805a2780c.gif[/img]

Thanks to anyone who still gives a crap about ASTRALODE Freeminers! Be sure to report any bugs you find [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1273010/discussions/0/2523653167134915687/]on the Steam community forums over here[/url], and please share whatever suggestions or feedback you have :)

- Drixxel

notes.title: ASTRALODE Freeminers Released! (v0.90 patch notes + roadmap)
notes.content:
Alright, ASTRALODE Freeminers is live! Thanks for taking a look at this asteroid mining puzzle thing, hope you have a bit of fun harvesting ores and generally pummeling the heck out of wild space rocks :D

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/37ea204638034780dc295d88e021f1caf4bac40b.gif[/img]

There are inevitably going to be a number of minor bugs and rough edges to smooth out which I'll be patching up as the week goes on, so please do report anything you find on the forums over here: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1273010/discussions/0/2523653167134915687/.

As it stands right now, Freeminers is a stable and self-contained 1/3rd chunk of the full ASTRALODE, but launching as v0.90 leaves a bit of room to grow. Plus, there are a number of cool features in the pipeline for this standalone free version! :)

I've decided to add the rest of the Azimuth Starminers to the roster available in Freeminers, building onto the opening 3-piece of Griff, Lorelei and Tentax. Each of the locked copilots will require certain conditions to be met in order to be unlocked, which you'll be able to sleuth out by visiting the Mellodeck and chatting with the crew.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/1f6e012bc623e184da9a1bde6373cb49988ac16b.gif[/img]

The Mellodeck is part of Azimuth HQ along with the Garage and Data-Dex, that whole wing of the main menu will become available in future updates. Your $core is being saved along with the rest of your player profile right now in Freeminers, though, so when the Garage is ready to be opened, you'll have cash to spend.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/5725c34bf1ff4d50a2e080b5efe2f9761fb61a41.gif[/img]

Also, once I've gotten all of ASTRALODE full's achievements planned out, I'll be adding Steam achievements to Freeminers that sync up with everything involving arcade mode. Oh yeah, and the game's soundtrack will be available on the store here hopefully by the end of the week!

Anyhow, cheers for having a peek at ASTRALODE Freeminers! Thanks for playing, and feel free to join this freshly-created Discord if you're into it :) https://discord.gg/EQRNHsq

- Drixxel

notes.title: ASTRALODE Dev Update #5
notes.content:
Hello! In this dev update, I'll be going into the details of each of the 10 standard power-ups available in ASTRALODE :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/2c0726c585331d5201e842977353117dc45cb2e8.gif[/img]


As covered in update #4, power-ups are earned by either harvesting ore or getting long (10+) chains, both of which contribute to your p-meter. Fill the p-meter and you'll be presented with a randomized selection of consumable power-ups to pick from. In addition, each of ASTRALODE's 10 copilots bring one power-up each with them into the run.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/3046cb0369a992f3de597d0b355556811fb3e210.gif[/img]

[h3]Restorefier[/h3]
All burnt ore is reset back to green grade (burnt rare ore is made whole again)

[h3]Goldenizer[/h3]
All unburnt ore is pushed forward to golden grade (unburnt rare ore is unaffected)

[h3]Defreezinator[/h3]
All frozen chunks are thawed

[h3]Stroidquaker[/h3]
All thawed chunks receive 1 damage

[h3]Blunder Cleaner[/h3]
Wipes out the current lost tools tally

[h3]Rock Roller[/h3]
Forces the asteroid to rotate or flip however chosen

[h3]Tractor Bomb[/h3]
An energy cone that harvests all ore on contact

[h3]Annihilazer[/h3]
A horizontal beam that instantly destroys all chunks in a row

[h3]Disinteshaver[/h3]
A vertical beam that instantly destroys all chunks in a column

[h3]Lazer Boomer[/h3]
An energy explosion that instantly destroys all chunks in a 4-quadrant pattern

So the Steam Game Festival is just around the corner! From June 16th and lasting for the duration of the festival, there'll be a demo of ASTRALODE available to check out. Definitely excited to get something out on Steam for people to play :)

- Drixxel

notes.title: ASTRALODE Dev Update #4
notes.content:
Hello! So in this dev update, I'll quickly run through ASTRALODE's chain scoring system and power-up cycle. The two of these are quite closely linked, so let's get into it :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/6a9a12c0de1dbf04da5de74adddea356e9d93cc7.gif[/img]

During Arcade mode, the green clock-lookin' thing hanging in space to the right of your mining vessel is the P-Meter. Each ore harvested caused your P-Meter to tick up a point, and when your P-Meter is completely filled at 12 points, you'll earn yourself a consumable power-up. Another way to fill your P-Meter involves stringing together unbroken chains of tools, where every 10 consecutive tools that earn $core (without ruining any ore or getting shot off into space) add 1 point to your P-Meter. So, let's imagine you launch 20 tools in a row without making even one dud move in that sequence - that'll add 2 points to your P-Meter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/f79b0dbc598e904436a378f547e4e9635723c479.gif[/img]

Once your P-Meter is completely filled to the 12-point mark, your copilot will bring the mining vessel around and park beside a random assortment of power-ups for you to pick from. Choosing from this selection will add that chosen power-up to one of your open power-up slots. In the event that your power-up slots are all occupied, you'll have the choice of either replacing one of your currently held power-ups with a new one from the random spread OR opting to skip picking a new power-up altogether, causing your P-Meter to blow and converting some of that energy directly into a semi-random amount of $core.

Also, just a heads up that there's been a bit of a scheduling change with the upcoming Steam Game Festival that has affected ASTRALODE Freeminer's release! It was announced last Friday that the Steam Game Festival has been postponed a week, which mucks up the plans for Freeminers just a smidge since I intended to have it released just as the Game Festival ended. As a result, Freeminers is now set to launch on June 23rd, just as the gamefest comes to a close. ASTRALODE will be participating in the Steam Game Festival with a playable demo, though, so on June 16th you'll be able to give it a try!

Anyhow, thanks for checking out ASTRALODE. In the next update, maybe I'll go into the specifics of what each of the 10 power-ups do. We shall see! Take care and all the best,

- Drixxel

notes.title: ASTRALODE Dev Update #3
notes.content:
Hello! So I thought it might be useful to go a little into how ore upgrading works in ASTRALODE. It's a major part of playing like a pro in Arcade mode, and anyone who wants to maximize their score is going to want to upgrade as much ore as they can :)

There are 4 grades of standard ore:

Green (worth 10 $core)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/3a501815d2081ba0c7fae035816c2044599c5d4c.png[/img]

Pale (worth 20 $core)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/6f5c1bee42c49138253a24c730c678882ae1e061.png[/img]

Golden (worth 30 $core)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/891f1d38b2a15dee66dbed258c8fd056ab544600.png[/img]

Burnt (worth 5 $core)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/5d404a6d864b8d06b69d08ff5beb559219945f49.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/f6f5150350b75829a0eb2ca029860fec90178e7f.gif[/img]

Ore that gets hit by an explosion will be pushed into it's next grade, starting from Green and ending in Burnt. As you can see by the point totals shown above, there's a sweet spot at the Golden ore grade that you don't want to overshoot if it can be at all avoided!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/e84637a682744edf1b701bef2743df66b1d4318b.gif[/img]

It's not all hopeless if an ore gets a lil' toasty, though. One of the starter power-ups, the Restorenizer, refreshes all Burnt ore in the asteroid you're currently mining back to Green.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/d3ef62ce1417bda933ba9c7586577c0a1eecad04.gif[/img]

In order to actually realize the value of an ore, it must be harvested by a grabber. The frequency by which grabbers appear in your randomly generated tool clusters depends on how much mining progress you've made on the current asteroid, with the likelihood of grabbers increasing as more chunks are mined away and as the ratio of ore-to-chunks rises. Any ore hit by a grabber is harvested, and both the ore and the grabber are removed from play when that happens.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/2d47befea8dcfbe6d7d8d5007da4647b69255587.gif[/img]

Rare ores, which as their name suggests will only rarely be amongst a given asteroid's ore allotment, start at their maximum value grade (worth a hefty 50 $core) and will be pushed into Burnt state after only a single hit by an explosion. Burnt Rares (worth a mere 5 $core, like their non-Rare brethren) can be refreshed back to their full value through the use of a Restorenizer. Also, Rare ore collectors need not worry if they harvest a Burnt Rare - that particular Rare's harvest record will still enter into the Atlas Mineralis just the same as if it were harvested uncooked.

That's all for now! I think a rundown of chain scoring and the power-up unlock cycle would be a good candidate for the next post. Until then, cheers for taking a look at ASTRALODE :)

- Drixxel

notes.title: ASTRALODE Dev Update #2
notes.content:
Hey! Just wanted to quickly run through a little of how ASTRALODE's Arcade mode works, as it's nice to have a more detailed written description of what's going on in screenshots and video :)

So an Arcade run starts by selecting your copilot from among those you've unlocked. Only a few are available from first launch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/b9e8a2e1f05548454556a0ebe504b8750eb42e53.png[/img]

Your copilot determines which power-up you start the run with, and they'll comment on your run as certain milestones are met. All ore harvested while running with a copilot contributes to their level, which results in an increasingly fancy badge displayed next to their name and a general warming up to you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/c156f0aa121f38858006762f2e4e3a4deb954d05.png[/img]

Once the run begins, you'll be presented with a randomized asteroid loaded with ore. Your copilot-determined power-up is here hanging out to the right of your mining vessel, and a preview of your first tool cluster is projected in the mouth of your vessel's tool generator.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/5cfcbeff47fa9c9c210066b5c21e69d8db3e1b44.gif[/img]

The game plays out in a self-paced, quasi-turn-based fashion as you chip away at the asteroid, one generated cluster of mining tools at a time. At random intervals, the asteroid will rotate 90 degrees and you'll be presented with a new face of the formation to mine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/75af00dd096ebc9cd2cba99ffac52c7ac7dff245.gif[/img]

An asteroid is cleared when all of its ore has been removed, ideally by safely harvesting it rather than ruining it with misplaced tools! Ruined ore sticks with you and ruining 4 total will end the run. Similarly, casting tools into space will end your run if a total of 8 tools are lost, but unlike ruined ore, this count resets at the start of the next asteroid.

So that's the basic rundown of how a typical Arcade mode level plays out! This doesn't touch on ore upgrading, the power-up cycle, rare ore collection, performance bonuses, etc., but I'll be getting into more of that in a later post :)

Also, just wanted to provide a quick update on release date stuff! The Steam Game Festival is coming up in June and ASTRALODE will be participating in that with a playable demo. This has slightly gummed up my scheduled plans for Freeminers - I've decided to push its release until after the Steam Game Festival as it would be too confusing, IMO, to have a free version and a demo version out simultaneously when they'll pretty much contain identical content. Also, this will give me time to tidy some things up and incorporate more player feedback. I've gotten things set up such that your save file will carry forward from the demo, so any time put in there won't be wasted.

Anyhow, thanks for checking out ASTRALODE! Looking forward to getting the demo out there for everyone who wants to give the game a shot :D

- Drixxel

notes.content:
Hello! Thanks for checking out ASTRALODE Freeminers :)

This thing's getting close to release ready, and you might have noted on the store page, the planned launch for ASTRALODE Freeminers is coming up quick. That May 28th release may end up getting pushed back just a smidge, maybe a week or two to allow me enough time to add more to the metagame and tighten some technical things up, but the core game is thoroughly tested, rock solid and ready to play. Have a peek at this handful of GIFs showcasing how the game's looking right now.

Copilot selection:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37179176/e0fac3418fb0729250104a8dde6e80d6d761e62a.gif[/img]

If there's anyone here on Steam who's interested in getting pre-release access to make their mark on the game's leaderboard, that'd be awesome and I'd really appreciate it. ASTRALODE Freeminers is going to be totally free, so you'll just be getting pre-release access to a free game, but let me know if you're into the idea of jumping the queue and lending a hand!

[h3][b]So, want to help test the ASTRALODE Freeminers leaderboard?[/b] Just shoot an email to trevor@drixxelsoft.com or leave a comment here or elsewhere on the forums letting me know you're interested! :)[/h3]

Cheers and all the best,
